capitals.name: Tikal (Yax Mutal)
capitals.note: The kingdom was called Mutul. Gazetteer coordinates of Tikal.

correction.text: Tikal and its immediate land (the city covers more than 16 km2; earthworks enclose about 120 km2)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Tikal row; its Maya envelope covers the area). The Tikal page: 'the dynasty was founded by Yax Ehb Xook, perhaps in the 1st century AD'; the city 'covered an area greater than 16 square kilometers'. The 15 km radius is only what the grid can show, not a page figure; there is no infobox area.

correction.text: Tikal's core territory, 'at least 25 kilometers in every direction', with Uaxactun absorbed

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'By the middle of the 5th century, Tikal had a core territory of at least 25 kilometers in every direction', and 'Uaxactun, together with smaller towns in the region, were absorbed into Tikal's kingdom' (undated). Drawn as 30 km. Dos Pilas (629) leaves by the split of 629 and the Caracol vassalage is a ledger overlay, not part of this core.

region.text: Tikal and its immediate land (the city covers more than 16 km2; earthworks enclose about 120 km2)

ledger.note: About 50: the Tikal dynasty is founded. 'The dynasty was founded by Yax Ehb Xook, perhaps in the 1st century AD'; the kingdom was 'simply called Mutul' and the city Yax Mutal. The year is the middle of the page's '1st century AD'; Tikal was 'already a significant city by around 350 BC' (Maya civilization).

region.text: Caracol, the client state of Tikal

ledger.note: 331: Caracol, founded this year, begins as a client of Tikal. 'The Caracol was officially founded in AD 331 by Te' K'ab Chaak' and 'was at first a client state of the more powerful city of Tikal'; the page does not date the client relation, so the founding year is used.

region.text: the land round Tikal, with Uaxactun, added to the core

ledger.note: About 450: Tikal's core grows to 25 km and more in every direction. 'By the middle of the 5th century, Tikal had a core territory of at least 25 kilometers in every direction'; 'Uaxactun, together with smaller towns in the region, were absorbed into Tikal's kingdom' (page gives no year for Uaxactun, which lies about 20 km north).

562: Calakmul and Caracol defeat Tikal and Caracol leaves Tikal's orbit. 'Tikal's comprehensive defeat at the hands of Calakmul and the Caracol polity in AD 562' (Tikal page); after 561 Calakmul's Sky Witness 'became the overlord of the city of Caracol', 'previously a Tikal vassal' (Calakmul page), and the defeat began 'a 130-year hiatus for Tikal'.

region.text: Dos Pilas, 'some 110 kilometers to the southwest' of Tikal

ledger.note: 629: Tikal founds Dos Pilas. 'In AD 629, the Tikal king K'inich Muwaan Jol II installed his son Balaj Chan K'awiil, aged four, as ruler of Dos Pilas'; the Tikal page: 'In 629, Tikal founded Dos Pilas, some 110 kilometers (68 mi) to the southwest.' The new state is dos-pilas.

region.text: Dos Pilas, 'some 110 kilometers to the southwest' of Tikal

ledger.note: 672: Tikal captures Dos Pilas. 'King Nuun Ujol Chaak of Tikal attacked and captured Dos Pilas in AD 672, driving B'alaj Chan K'awiil into a five-year exile, probably in Calakmul.'

region.text: Dos Pilas, 'some 110 kilometers to the southwest' of Tikal

ledger.note: 677: Dos Pilas is free again. 'This exile was only ended in AD 677, on the same day that Calakmul celebrated a success over Tikal'; in 679 Dos Pilas defeated Tikal ('a humiliating defeat by its smaller rival').

region.text: Tikal's core territory, 'at least 25 kilometers in every direction', with Uaxactun absorbed

ledger.note: 869: the last monument of Tikal. Stela 11 was 'dedicated in 869 by Jasaw Chan K'awiil II. This was the last monument erected at Tikal before the city finally fell into silence'; 'culminating with the site's abandonment by the end of the 10th century' and 'after 950, Tikal was all but deserted'. The end year is the last monument, not a conquest.

wars.name: Intervention of Teotihuacan at Tikal
wars.outcome: On 14 January 378 Siyaj K'ak' arrived and the Tikal king Chak Tok Ich'aak died; no territory is recorded as changing hands.
wars.note: 'These recorded events strongly suggest that Siyaj K'ak' led a Teotihuacan invasion that defeated the native Tikal king.' Not drawn as a contest: Teotihuacan lay about 1,000 km away and no page gives land.

wars.name: Tikal-Caracol axe war
wars.outcome: Tikal 'enacted a ch'ak (axe) war and defeated Caracol' in 556; Caracol took revenge in 562.
wars.note: No land changed hands on the page.

wars.name: Calakmul-Caracol defeat of Tikal
wars.outcome: Tikal was defeated and its king sacrificed in 562 ('Sky Witness defeated Tikal itself and sacrificed its king'); Caracol left Tikal's orbit and a 130-year hiatus began.
wars.note: Tikal's core stayed Tikal's; the ledger records the end of the Caracol vassalage.

wars.name: Tikal-Dos Pilas war

zones.text: Dos Pilas, 'some 110 kilometers to the southwest' of Tikal

wars.outcome: Tikal captured Dos Pilas in 672 and held it, driving the king into exile, until 677; in 679 Dos Pilas defeated Tikal.
wars.note: Calakmul's role: the exile was 'probably in Calakmul' and ended the day Calakmul 'celebrated a success over Tikal'.

wars.name: Tikal-Calakmul battle of 695
wars.outcome: In August 695 Jasaw Chan K'awiil I defeated Calakmul in 'a catastrophic battle'; Tikal 'was able to turn the tables on its great rival'. The Tikal page: 'in 695, he captured the enemy noble and threw the enemy state into a long decline.'
wars.note: No border is given; Tikal's recovery after 695 is not dated on the pages.

certainty.note: Classic Maya kingdoms had no fixed borders; the core radii are the grid's minimum, not measured frontiers.

notes:
NEW STATE. Cliopatria has no Tikal row; it is a kingdom inside the 'Mayan City-States' envelope (-247..849) and the 'Later' row to 959. Start 50 is the middle of 'perhaps in the 1st century AD' (confidence 2).
RADII. The page's only extent figures are the 120 km2 earthworks, 'at least 25 kilometers in every direction' by about 450 and the Dos Pilas colony 110 km away; the 15 and 30 km radii are the smallest the 250 km2 grid cells can show.
HIATUS. The 130-year hiatus after 562 (and Tikal's recovery after 695) are not territorial on any page opened; no events. Tikal's rule over Naranjo, Yaxha, Uaxactun and Dos Pilas after 695 is page-silent; Naranjo is not described as subordinate on the Tikal page (the Caracol page says Tikal lost Naranjo 'to rival Calakmul' in the mid-sixth century).
NOT DRAWN. Teotihuacan 378 is a war with no zone. Dzibanche page (Kaan origin) would not load.
COUNTERPARTS WITHOUT DOSSIER. Uaxactun (absorbed into Tikal, undated), Naranjo, Yaxha.
